checklists.title: Opening checklist
checklists.desc: Before the first customer. Takes about 15 minutes.

items.t: Staff on shift are fit to work, in clean uniform, hair covered; no one with vomiting, diarrhoea or fever handling food
Food-handler medical certificates for everyone on shift are valid (check expiry dates)
Hand-wash station has soap, warm water and single-use towels
Chiller temperature (0 to 4°C; act above 5°C)
Freezer temperature (-18°C or colder; act above -15°C)
Scale tested with the test weight and the county weights-and-measures stamp is valid
Colour-coded boards and knives in place (red raw meat, yellow poultry, blue fish, white cooked)
Sanitiser mixed at label strength; chemicals in the closed cupboard
Floors, drains, tables and blocks clean; no pests or droppings seen
Meat labels checked: first in, first out; nothing past its sell-by or freeze-by day on display
Opening till float counted (KSh)
Online orders portal open; overnight orders acknowledged; sold-out items correct
Fire extinguisher and fire blanket in place (grill branches)
Handover notes from the last shift read (write anything important)
Chiller temperature (0 to 4°C; act above 5°C)
Freezer temperature (-18°C or colder; act above -15°C)
Hot-holding temperature of cooked food (60°C or above); write the lowest reading
Cooked food on display is within 2 hours of the hold start; older food discarded and logged
Probe core temperatures taken and logged for each grill batch (74°C poultry and mince, 71°C pork, 63°C beef/goat/fish)
Hands washed and boards/knives sanitised between species and after every long pause
Every online order acknowledged within 5 minutes; no order waiting more than 45 minutes after packing
Allergy flags on today's orders checked and marked
Waste so far today (kg)

checklists.title: Closing checklist
checklists.desc: At the end of the day or the end of your shift.

items.t: Chiller temperature (0 to 4°C; act above 5°C)
Freezer temperature (-18°C or colder; act above -15°C)
Chilled meat that was above 5°C for more than 2 hours has been discarded and logged
Boards, knives, saw, scale, mincer, floors and drains cleaned and sanitised; cleaning sheet signed
Bins emptied and washed; waste removed
Leftover cooked food labelled, cooled within the limits or discarded; nothing unlabelled kept
Waste for the whole day (kg)
Counted cash at close (KSh)
Cash-up submitted in Operations and M-Pesa messages matched to orders
Unfinished orders handed over and written in the notes; sold-out items updated
Doors, windows and cold-room locked; alarm set; equipment off where required
Handover note for the next shift (problems, stock to order, repairs)

checklists.title: Weekly checklist
checklists.desc: Once a week, by the manager.

items.t: Chiller and freezer shelves emptied, cleaned and sanitised; walls and ceiling wiped
Defrost freezers if frost is thick; temperature recovered within 2 hours
Supplier licences and meat inspection certificates on file and not expired (check monthly)
Medical certificates: list anyone due within 30 days
Pest-control visit or bait check done and logged
Fire extinguisher gauge in the green; staff know where it is
Thermometers checked in ice water (0°C) and boiling water (about 100°C); replace any off by more than 1°C
Complaints and refunds this week reviewed; three of the same kind in 30 days reported to head office
Data backup downloaded and a copy kept (Operations > Backups or cPanel backup)
Anything to escalate to Azizo head office (support ticket)

courses.title: Receiving meat and the cold chain

pts: Buy only from licensed abattoirs or suppliers; keep the licence copy and check expiry every month.
No stamped inspection certificate or delivery note means no acceptance.
Check the vehicle, the meat (colour, smell, slime, texture) and the core temperature.
Chilled meat is accepted at 4°C or below and rejected above 7°C. Frozen meat is accepted at -15°C or below.
Record date, supplier, species, kg, temperature, accepted or rejected, and your name. Move to cold storage within 15 minutes.
Chillers 0 to 4°C; freezers -18°C or colder. Log at opening, midday and closing.
Raw below, cooked above; red meat, poultry and fish kept apart; nothing on the floor.
First in, first out. Beef, goat and pork: sell or freeze within 3 days; poultry and mince 2 days; fish 1 day.
Never refreeze thawed meat; thaw only in the chiller.
Power cut: doors shut, tell the manager, discard chilled meat above 5°C for more than 2 hours.

quiz.q: A delivery of chilled beef measures 6°C at the core and has a valid certificate. What do you do?
o: Reject it: acceptance is 4°C or below (reject above 7°C), so call the manager and record the reading
Accept it if the driver agrees
quiz.why: 4°C or below is accepted and above 7°C is rejected. At 6°C you must not accept on your own: record it and call the manager, who decides under the SOP.

quiz.q: Which delivery paperwork is required?
o: A stamped meat inspection certificate or delivery note
Nothing if you know the supplier
quiz.why: No paper, no acceptance.

quiz.q: What is the freezer target temperature?
quiz.why: Freezers are kept at -18°C or colder; above -15°C means act and log.

quiz.q: How long can fresh poultry and mince be kept before sale or freezing?
quiz.why: Poultry and mince: 2 days. Beef, goat and pork: 3 days. Fish: 1 day.

quiz.q: The power is out. The chiller has been above 5°C for 3 hours. What now?
o: Sell it quickly at a discount
Discard the chilled meat and log it
quiz.why: Chilled meat above 5°C for more than 2 hours is discarded and logged.

pts: Red = raw red meat, yellow = poultry, blue = fish, white = cooked.
Wash and sanitise boards, knives and the saw between species and after any pause longer than 30 minutes.
Keep out of the chiller only what you can cut in 20 minutes.
Test the scale each morning; the county stamp must be valid. Tare the tray and weigh in front of the customer.
Label every pack: product, weight, date, branch.
Wash hands for 20 seconds with soap and warm water on arrival, after the toilet, after raw meat, waste, phones or money, and before ready-to-eat food.
Clean apron, hair covering, closed non-slip shoes; short clean nails; no jewellery other than a plain band.
Cuts covered with a blue waterproof plaster and a glove.
If you have diarrhoea, vomiting, fever or infected skin, do not handle food and tell the manager the same day. Return after 48 hours with no symptoms.
Valid food-handler medical certificate, renewed every 6 months.

quiz.q: Which board colour is for poultry?
quiz.why: Yellow is poultry.

quiz.q: How long should you wash your hands?
o: 20 seconds with soap and warm water
quiz.why: 20 seconds, soap, warm water, single-use towel.

quiz.q: You have had diarrhoea since last night. What do you do?
o: Tell the manager and do not handle food; return after 48 hours with no symptoms
quiz.why: Illness must be reported the same day and you stay off food handling until 48 hours symptom-free.

quiz.q: When must the scale be tested?
o: Each morning with a test weight
quiz.why: Each morning, and the county stamp must be valid.

quiz.q: How often must a food handler's medical certificate be renewed?
quiz.why: The SOP requires renewal every 6 months, as required by the county.

pts: Remove debris, wash with detergent, rinse, apply sanitiser at label strength, leave for the contact time.
After every shift: tables, blocks, knives, saw, scale, mincer, floors, drains. Daily: chillers wiped, bins washed. Weekly: shelves emptied and cleaned. Monthly: deep clean, drains descaled.
Cloths are single-use or colour-coded and washed hot daily; mops kept out of the food area.
Chemicals stay in a labelled closed cupboard. Never put them in drink bottles.
The supervisor signs the cleaning sheet each shift.

quiz.q: What is the correct order?
quiz.why: Remove soil first. Sanitiser does not work well on dirty surfaces.

quiz.q: Where do cleaning chemicals belong?
o: In a drink bottle near the sink
In a labelled, closed cupboard away from food
quiz.why: Labelled, closed, away from food. Never decanted into drink bottles.

quiz.q: Who signs the cleaning sheet?
quiz.why: The supervisor signs each shift.

quiz.q: You see rat droppings in the store. What now?
o: Record it, tell the manager at once, and clean and sanitise; the manager arranges pest control
quiz.why: Report it, clean and sanitise, and get pest control arranged and logged.

quiz.q: How often are chiller and freezer shelves emptied and cleaned?
quiz.why: Weekly, with the deep clean monthly.

pts: Acknowledge every online order within 5 minutes and keep the status honest.
Weigh, label and pack to the order; raw meat packed separately; ice packs for journeys over 30 minutes.
A second person checks orders above KSh 5,000 before handover.
Riders: clean insulated bag, helmet and reflective jacket, call the customer 5 minutes before arrival.
Out of stock: tell the customer before substituting and mark the item sold out immediately.
Listen, apologise, record order number and photo. Do not argue.
Replace or refund within 24 hours. Quality and safety complaints are always accepted.
Illness complaint: stop selling the batch, keep samples, note batch and supplier, raise an urgent support ticket.
Three complaints of the same kind in 30 days trigger an unannounced inspection.

quiz.q: Within what time must you acknowledge an online order?
quiz.why: Within 5 minutes.

quiz.q: Above what order value does a second person check before handover?
quiz.why: Orders above KSh 5,000 get a second check.

quiz.q: A customer says the meat made them ill. First action?
o: Stop selling that batch, keep samples, record batch and supplier, raise an urgent ticket
quiz.why: Stop the batch, keep samples, and tell head office immediately.

quiz.q: How soon should a replacement or refund be given for a valid complaint?
quiz.why: Within 24 hours.

quiz.q: An item is out of stock. What do you do?
o: Tell the customer first and mark it sold out in the portal
quiz.why: Tell the customer before substituting and update the portal at once.

pts: Cook only fresh or properly thawed meat; marinate in the chiller.
Core temperatures held 15 seconds: poultry and mince 74°C; pork 71°C; beef and goat 63°C with a 3-minute rest; fish 63°C; sausages 74°C.
Separate tongs, boards and plates for raw and cooked; wash the probe between uses.
Keep fuel away from food; extinguisher and fire blanket near the grill.
Hot food at 60°C or above and discarded 2 hours after the hold begins.
The danger zone is 5 to 60°C; never more than 2 hours in total.
Cool from 60°C to 21°C within 2 hours and then to 5°C within 4 more hours.
Reheat once only, to 74°C throughout. Unlabelled food is never sold.

quiz.q: What core temperature must chicken reach?
quiz.why: Poultry and mince reach 74°C.

quiz.q: At what temperature must hot food be held?
quiz.why: 60°C or above, discarded 2 hours after the hold begins.

quiz.q: How many times may food be reheated?
quiz.why: Once only, to 74°C throughout.

quiz.q: How long may food stay in the 5 to 60°C danger zone in total?
quiz.why: No more than 2 hours in total.

quiz.q: Leftover cooked meat in the chiller must be used within:
quiz.why: Within 24 hours, labelled.

courses.title: Allergens, packaging and dispatch
courses.for_roles: Grill and kitchen staff, packers, riders

pts: Main allergens: milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, peanuts and tree nuts, soy, wheat or gluten, sesame, sulphites.
Keep an allergen list per dish and review it when a recipe or supplier changes.
Never guess: say "I will check". Use separate utensils, clean hands and fresh oil for an allergic customer and mark the order.
Emergency (swelling, trouble breathing): call 112 or 999 and stay with the person.
Clean, food-grade, leak-proof containers; do not reuse single-use packaging.
Tamper-evident sticker with dish name, time packed and "Eat within 2 hours".
Hand over in a clean insulated bag; hot at 60°C or above, cold at 5°C or below.
Check items, sauces, cutlery, notes and the allergy flag against the ticket. Remake if more than 45 minutes after packing.

quiz.q: A customer asks if a dish has peanuts and you are not sure. You say:
quiz.why: Never guess about allergens.

quiz.q: A customer shows swelling and trouble breathing after eating. First action?
o: Call 112 or 999 and stay with them
quiz.why: This is an emergency: call at once.

quiz.q: What must be on a takeaway label?
o: Dish name, time packed, "Eat within 2 hours", and allergens present
quiz.why: Dish name, time and allergens, with a tamper-evident sticker.

quiz.q: A packed order has waited 60 minutes before dispatch. What now?
o: Remake it: the cap is 45 minutes from packing
quiz.why: Beyond 45 minutes from packing, remake the order.

quiz.q: Hot food is handed to the rider at:
quiz.why: 60°C or above for cooked food.

pts: Run the opening checklist before the first customer: health, temperatures, scale, sanitiser, labels, float, orders portal.
Mid-shift: temperatures, hot-holding, probe logs, orders under 5 minutes.
Closing: temperatures, cleaning sheet, waste, count cash, submit the cash-up, hand over notes, lock up.
Any critical item that fails needs a written action. The manager reviews the failures daily.
Cash-up goes in every evening; M-Pesa messages are matched to orders; a gap above the tolerance is explained the same day.

quiz.q: When do you run the opening checklist?
quiz.why: Before the first customer.

quiz.q: A critical checklist item fails. What must you do?
o: Write down the action you took
quiz.why: Failures need a written corrective action and the manager reviews them.

quiz.q: When is the cash-up submitted?
quiz.why: Every evening at closing.

quiz.q: Who is told about a cash gap above tolerance?
quiz.why: The manager must be told and the gap explained the same day.

quiz.q: What is written in the handover note?
o: Problems, stock to order, repairs and unfinished orders
quiz.why: Anything the next shift needs to know.

courses.title: Brand standards and escalation
courses.for_roles: Everyone, especially managers and franchise owners

pts: The same look, wording, prices guidance, uniforms and cleanliness in every branch: customers must meet the same Azizo everywhere.
Use only the approved logo, colours and signage from the brand pack; no changes without written approval.
Never make health, sourcing or price claims that Azizo has not approved.
Escalate by support ticket in Operations: normal issues in a day; urgent issues (illness, recall, fire, theft, data breach) at once by phone and ticket.

quiz.q: May a branch change the logo colours?
o: No: only approved brand-pack assets, with written approval for changes
quiz.why: Only the approved brand pack.

quiz.q: A customer reports illness after eating. How do you escalate?
o: Urgently: phone head office and raise an urgent ticket
quiz.why: Urgent issues go by phone and ticket at once.

quiz.q: May a branch advertise "100% organic" without approval?
o: No: claims must be approved and true
quiz.why: Unapproved health or sourcing claims are not allowed.

quiz.q: Where are normal issues raised?
quiz.why: Raise a support ticket.

quiz.q: Why does brand consistency matter?
o: Customers must trust the same standard in every branch
quiz.why: Trust in one branch carries across all of them.

manual.t: Business permit and public health licence or certificate displayed (county)
Meat supplier agreements and licences on file (abattoir, inspection certificates)
Scale verified and stamped by weights and measures
Thermometers and temperature probes checked and working
Fire extinguisher serviced and staff shown how to use it
All staff have a valid food-handler medical certificate
Payment test done: cash, M-Pesa prompt and receipt
Signage, uniforms and brand pack in place
Cold-room temperature held for 24 hours before stocking meat
